calibration.reference_10: Seeing Theory (Brown) 'Regression Analysis / Correlation' chapter and Bartosz Ciechanowski's explainers: the chart is the page, labels never collide at any width, every manipulation is answered by an on-chart change the eye can follow.
calibration.reference_8: BBC Bitesize GCSE Statistics 'Misleading graphs' / 'Sampling' revision + test pages, with GOV.UK Design System accessibility (two-colour focus indicator, tables that reflow on a phone, every chart with a legend and a data table).

caps_triggered.evidence: shot-a1-framing-mobile.png (chart, y≈690–760): the end-of-line value labels '73.6' and '71.8' are drawn on top of each other and run past the SVG's right edge (label x = 596+10 with a 22px font in a 640-unit viewBox), so they read as one unreadable glyph mash and are cut off; the axis title 'score out of 100' at y=14 with a 22px font has its ascenders clipped by the SVG top edge and sits on top of the '100' tick label. Same collisions at 768 and 1280 (shot-a1-framing-tablet.png, shot-a1-framing-desktop.png top-left and right end of the chart), and in a2/a3 at 360 the axis titles 'mean sleep (hours)' and 'sunburn clinic visits / week' are clipped at the top and overlap the top tick; a3's x-axis title 'ice-cream tubs sold / week' overlaps the '200'/'400' tick labels (shot-a3-correlation-mobile.png). Live check at 360 confirmed the a1 chart renders at 279×158 px.

verdict: The lesson's tone, keyboard path, live regions, data tables and honest nuance are close to the 7 rung, and I completed all three activities and the case file keyboard-only at 360 px with no page overflow and zero network requests. But the Activity 1 chart, the object the whole activity is about, ships with overlapping and clipped labels at every captured width, a CSS bug that fills the line series into solid wedges when zoomed, no legend, and 8–10 px text at 360 and 1280; that is a layout break in the lesson's core visual. Beyond the cap, the authored focus ring measures 2.4:1 against the paper background (WCAG 1.4.11 needs 3:1) despite the report claiming verified contrast, and the brief's 'justified conclusion' is optional in practice.

blocking.issue: Activity 1 chart is broken as a picture: end labels overlap and clip, axis title clipped and over the top tick, polylines filled by CSS into spurious wedges when zoomed, no legend, and the chart is a 279×158 px thumbnail at 360 and ~425 px with 8.6 px text at 1280.
blocking.where: app.js:108-149 (renderA1Chart), styles.css:117-135 (.chart-wrap, .series-a/.series-b, mobile tick sizes); shot-a1-framing-mobile.png chart region; live 360 px with 'Zoom 70–74' shows a filled rust wedge under Group A (computed fill rgb(162,59,42) on the polyline because .series-a { fill } overrides fill="none").
blocking.why_it_caps_score: Clipped, colliding text and a false filled shape in the core chart at all three captured viewports is a layout break in the one visual the activity exists to teach with.

blocking.issue: The authored focus indicator fails WCAG 2.2 AA non-text contrast: #ff7a00 measures 2.38:1 against the paper background and 2.61:1 against white cards (1.4.11 requires 3:1), and TEST_REPORT's contrast table omits it while claiming AA verification.
blocking.where: styles.css:50-51 (:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus) … box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px var(--paper) }), styles.css:21 (--focus: #ff7a00); live tab-through at 360 showed outline rgb(255,122,0) on every control; TEST_REPORT.md:71 lists no ratio for the ring.
blocking.why_it_caps_score: The brief's primary goal says 'no accessibility failure' and the definition of done says 'verified contrast ratios'; a focus ring that fails the numeric AA test on every control is a checkable failure a rubric judge will find in seconds.

blocking.issue: The brief's required inputs are optional in practice: Activity 3 marks the conclusion 'answered', reveals the headline builder and enables Finish with an empty justification, and Activity 2 accepts the keyed answer without a single sample ever being drawn — the longest option is the correct one in both, so a teen can finish without running either experiment.
blocking.where: app.js:296-303 (#a3-check handler: state.a3.answered = true regardless of just.length), app.js:240-246 (#a2-check: 'tried' only adds a tip); live run: picked 'third' with #a3-justify empty → 'Careful and correct.', #a3-headline shown, later #a3-next enabled with justification still empty.
blocking.why_it_caps_score: The primary goal is 'completes all three activities with meaningful input' and the must-have is 'a justified conclusion'; when neither the experiment nor the justification is required, a rubric judge records a missing deliverable and the learner gets a guessable quiz.

non_blocking.issue: Screen-reader chart description contains floating-point garbage: 'Group A rises from 71.19999999999999 to 73.6' (heard as a long string of nines after the learner moves a slider).
non_blocking.where: app.js:134 (`${FS.finalA - FS.riseA}` and `${fmt(FS.finalB - FS.riseB)}` — only the second is formatted); observed live after ArrowRight on #a1-min.

non_blocking.issue: The correlation coefficient r is never defined for the learner — the stat tile says 'Correlation, all 52 weeks (r): 0.82' and the exemplar says 'r ≈ 0.8' — while EDUCATOR_GUIDE.md:20 claims 'r is introduced as how tightly two things move together, from −1 to 1'. A Year 11 who has not met r has no scale for 0.82.
non_blocking.fix: index.html:193 — append to the lead: ' Statisticians measure how tightly two things move together with a number called r: it runs from −1 to 1, and the closer it is to 1, the more tightly the two rise together.' app.js:278 — stat label 'Correlation r, all 52 weeks (scale −1 to 1)'.

non_blocking.issue: Feedback says late-library students are 'around two-thirds of everyone leaving the library at 21:00', but the sampler pool is ~302 late + ~224 others ≈ 57%, and the 500-draw the feedback tells the learner to run shows 56.4%.
non_blocking.fix: Replace 'but around two-thirds of everyone leaving the library at 21:00' with 'but well over half of everyone leaving the library at 21:00 (about 57% in the long run — your draws will vary around that)'.

non_blocking.issue: The 'Sampling: convenience draws averaged…' notebook entry is written once (first time both methods exist) and never updated, so it freezes early small-sample numbers (e.g. 68.0% from one n=50 draw) in the case file.
non_blocking.fix: Add `function setNote(id, text) { const n = state.notebook.find(x => x.id === id); if (n) { n.text = text; save(); renderNotebook(); } else addNote(id, text); }` and call setNote('a2-compare', …) at app.js:236.

Add under each nav-row a helper: `

Answer the questions above to unlock the next check.

non_blocking.issue: Draw means outside 6.0–8.0 h are clamped to the axis edge without any marker, so an n=10 convenience draw with mean 5.8 h is drawn at exactly 6.0.
non_blocking.fix: Compute the axis from data: `const vals = draws.map(d => d.meanSleep).concat(P.meanSleep); const ymin = Math.min(6, Math.floor(Math.min(...vals) * 2) / 2), ymax = Math.max(8, Math.ceil(Math.max(...vals) * 2) / 2);`

keep: The three-way reflection question 'So is the zoomed chart dishonest?' (index.html:110-120) with its two specific counter-examples in app.js:174-181 — the hospital temperature chart for 'Too strict' and the computed 25× taller gap for 'Too relaxed' — teaches the non-zero-axis nuance honestly instead of the usual 'always start at zero'.

Feedback labels and voice: 'Not yet — have another look.', 'The other way round.', 'Check the table.', 'Almost.', 'That's the expert view.' — no scores, no attempt counters, no timers, unlimited retry; a 15-year-old is corrected without being shamed.

Focus management in go() (app.js:88-91): after every navigation focus lands on the new screen's h2 (tabindex=-1) and the page scrolls to top, with the skip link first in tab order and a body-level visually-hidden role=status announcer (app.js:64-66) reporting every state change ('Axis now 70 to 74…', 'Activity 1 complete. Next: Sampling is now available.').

The case-file review's honesty (model.js:95-105, app.js:349): it checks structure, evidence words and over-claiming words ('proves', 'definitely', 'never') and states plainly 'This review checks structure and wording only; it does not judge whether your reasoning is right — that is for you and your teacher to discuss.'

Start-screen privacy copy (index.html:52-53): 'stays in this browser only (nothing is sent anywhere). Use Reset at any time to wipe it' plus 'Every school, town, person and dataset here is fictional' — verified live: zero non-localhost requests, localStorage key removed on Reset.
gap_to_10: Seeing Theory (Brown) and Ciechanowski make the chart the page: it fills the width at every viewport, labels are laid out so they never collide, the legend is part of the drawing, and when the learner changes the axis the same points visibly stretch so the eye learns the lesson before the copy states it. Here the chart is a 279×158 px thumbnail under a control panel bigger than itself, with 9 px text and overlapping labels, and the pedagogy lives in the stat tiles and prose rather than in the picture.
